objections.claim: The online no-listener mechanism is unsound. It retains the host network namespace while claiming that `--unshare-ipc` and removal of pathname Unix sockets prevent SCM_RIGHTS imports because abstract Unix sockets are network-namespace-scoped. Since the online profile explicitly does not use `--unshare-net`, host abstract AF_UNIX peers remain reachable; `--unshare-ipc` does not isolate them. A descendant can create/connect an abstract Unix socket and receive an already-bound UDP descriptor via `recvmsg`/SCM_RIGHTS, then receive traffic without invoking any denied `socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM)`, `bind`, `listen`, or `accept` syscall. The stated SCM_RIGHTS regression therefore cannot establish the claimed kernel invariant. The plan must add kernel-enforced prevention of every post-launch descriptor-acquisition path in the online profile while preserving required egress—for example, deny AF_UNIX acquisition/SCM_RIGHTS plus equivalent descriptor-import mechanisms and isolate the PID/proc surface—and require adversarial regressions from a host abstract-socket peer before PD-001 can discharge.
